subject: Possible bug with using user-defined parameter set

messages.author: 2c921e34a21bba8b
messages.subject: Possible bug with using user-defined parameter set
parts:
Hi,

I might have found a bug in the program when using user-defined best parameter set. It seems like the first parameter in the file is not written to the respective input file. See the attached files. GW_DELAY.gw has not been updated in the *.gw files. All other listed parameters are correct in their corresponding input file.

messages.author: e28329d3e25e358e
messages.subject: Re: Possible bug with using user-defined parameter set
parts:
Hi Michael,

I have checked and I think this is NOT a bug.

So you have the best parameter values of GW_DELAY = 82.18 and you select the method of change is "ABSOLUTE", it means that you new values should be
new GW_DELAY = old GW_DELAY + 82.18 = 494.8140
I think in this case your old values is = 494.8140 - 82.18 = 412.6.  Could you check again?

messages.subject: Re: Possible bug with using user-defined parameter set
parts:
Hi Michael,

If you select the "Change" = "Replace", this will write the TxtInOut files with parameter values exactly equals to the ones that you given in the external file.

So the "Change" column is RELEVANT in this case. I made the code general to serve different needs (e.g., what if users want to change, for examples, CN2 value by X%, or increase X units, or replaced with X and with this X value is given in the external file => all of these are possible with the current code)

and R-SWAT does NOT skip any parameters in this case.

Does R-SWAT not update the first parameter in your case? If yes, could you share with me your (1) Parameter file, (2) RSWATproject.rds file and (3) TxtInOut files, I will check that
